headline: President Bush created an emergency board to look into a labor dispute between Philadelphia-area commuter rail operator SEPTA and its train conductors.
what_it_does: This order sets up a presidential emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) and its conductors, who are represented by the United Transportation Union. The board's job is to look into the dispute and report on it. Under federal railroad labor law, such boards are generally used to help settle disputes, and they usually delay strikes or lockouts while the process runs.

who_it_affects.group: SEPTA train conductors in the United Transportation Union
who_it_affects.how: Their labor dispute with SEPTA is reviewed by a federal board, which can delay any strike while the review happens.
The agency's dispute with its conductors goes before a federal board for investigation and a report.

who_it_affects.group: Commuter rail riders in the Philadelphia area
who_it_affects.how: They could see a delay in any possible work stoppage while the board does its work.

when_it_takes_effect: August 9, 2004, the date it was signed
